mainTopic: How much land the buyer gets when a sale document leaves out a boundary or uses unclear wording
overview: This amud opens by closing an earlier series of questions: the case of boundaries listed in an alternating pattern stays unresolved (תיקו). Next the גמרא asks about a sale document that lists three of a field's boundaries but leaves out the fourth. רב says the buyer gets everything except the strip along the fourth side. שמואל says he gets even that strip. רב אסי says he gets only one furrow along the named edges, because the seller held back the rest. רבא's ruling comes in two versions. One starts from רב's view and the other from שמואל's, and each adds conditions about whether the strip is 'swallowed' inside the other boundaries and whether it is important (a row of palm trees or a nine-קב area). The גמרא lists the cases where both versions agree and leaves the two mixed cases to the judges (שודא דדייני). The amud then turns to רבה's rulings on how the exact wording of a sale decides how much is sold. אביי challenges these rulings and רבה is silent. For the first ruling, bills of sale from רבה's house show that he kept his view. For the second, the people first conclude that both wordings give half, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What if the boundaries were listed in an alternating pattern?
steps.stepSummary: The last in a series of questions: what is the law when the seller listed the boundaries in an alternating, skipping pattern?
steps.simpleTranslation: If the seller listed the boundaries in an alternating way, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a series of questions about how a seller describes a field's boundaries. This last one asks about a skipping, alternating pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier questions dealt with other ways of listing the neighboring fields. Here the seller names some of the neighbors on each side and skips others. Does the buyer still get the whole field, or only part of it?

keyTerms.meaning: In an alternating or skipping pattern, with gaps
What is the law? (the standard way to open a question)

phrases.english: In an alternating pattern, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means the seller named some neighboring fields on each side and skipped others, back and forth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a series of questions from the previous part of the daf
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether listing boundaries in an alternating pattern limits what the buyer acquires

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finds no answer, so the question stands as תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand: no answer was found.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer and leaves the question open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו does not mean the question was a bad one. It means no proof was found either way, so the question stays undecided.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question raised in step 1
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The alternating-boundaries question is left unresolved.

steps.title: Three boundaries listed, the fourth left out: רב's view
steps.stepSummary: The seller listed three boundaries but not the fourth. רב says the buyer gets everything except the strip along the fourth boundary.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the seller wrote the first, second and third boundaries but did not write the fourth, רב says the buyer acquires the whole field except the fourth boundary strip.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case about a missing fourth boundary and gives רב's opinion first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A field has four sides, and a sale document usually names the neighbor on each side. רב says leaving out one side does not cancel the sale. The seller only kept back the edge strip, the furrow along that fourth side.

keyTerms.meaning: He marked out or listed a boundary
Boundary: the edge of the field, usually named by the neighboring field

phrases.english: If he listed for him the first boundary
and the second boundary and the third boundary,
but the fourth boundary he did not list for him:
רב said: he acquired everything,
except for the fourth boundary.
phrases.notes: He means the strip right along the fourth edge, not the whole fourth half of the field.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָצַר לוֹ מֶצֶר רִאשׁוֹן וּמֶצֶר שֵׁנִי וּמֶצֶר שְׁלִישִׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related case after the unresolved question
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The buyer acquires the entire field except the strip along the unlisted fourth boundary.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Except for the fourth boundary' does not mean the buyer loses a large section. It is only the narrow edge strip along that side.

steps.title: שמואל: the buyer gets even the fourth strip
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב and says the buyer acquires even the strip along the fourth boundary.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: the buyer acquires even the fourth boundary strip.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a second opinion that is more generous to the buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, leaving out the fourth boundary does not show that the seller kept anything back. The buyer gets the whole field, edge strip included.

phrases.english: And שמואל said: even the fourth boundary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with רב in the same case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The buyer acquires the whole field including the fourth boundary strip.

steps.title: רב אסי: only one furrow along the field
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי takes the strictest view: the buyer gets only a single furrow running along the listed boundaries.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: the buyer acquires only one furrow along the whole field.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion is given, the most limiting for the buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי says the buyer does not get the inside of the field at all. He only gets a one-furrow-wide strip running along the three boundaries that were listed.

keyTerms.meaning: A furrow: one plowed line in a field

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב אַסִּי אָמַר: לֹא קָנָה אֶלָּא
phrases.english: And רב אסי said: he acquired only
one furrow along the whole of it.
phrases.notes: He means a thin strip running along the edges the seller did name.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב אַסִּי אָמַר: לֹא קָנָה אֶלָּא תֶּלֶם אֶחָד עַל פְּנֵי כּוּלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third, stricter opinion to the argument
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The buyer acquires only one furrow's width along the three listed boundaries.

steps.title: Why רב אסי rules this way
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי agrees with רב that the seller kept something back. But he says that if the seller kept back part of one boundary, he kept back part of the whole field.
steps.simpleTranslation: He agrees with רב, who said the seller kept something back. And since he kept something back at the boundary, he also kept something back in all of the field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רב אסי's surprising opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and רב אסי share one idea: leaving out a boundary means the seller held something back. רב limits that to the edge strip. רב אסי pushes it further and says the seller held back the whole inside of the field, so only a furrow along the named edges is sold.

keyTerms.meaning: He definitely kept back part for himself

phrases.english: He holds like רב,
who said: he kept back part for himself;
and since he kept back at the boundary,
he also kept back in all of them.
phrases.notes: He means the seller kept back the inside of the whole field as well, not just the one edge.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַב, דְּאָמַר: שַׁיּוֹרֵי שַׁיַּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for רב אסי's view in step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב אסי accepts רב's idea that the seller kept something back, but extends it from one boundary to the entire field.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב and רב אסי share one starting idea and differ only in how far it reaches.

steps.title: רבא rules like רב
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the buyer acquires everything except the fourth boundary strip, like רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the הלכה is that the buyer acquires everything except the fourth boundary.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא settles the argument and decides the הלכה like רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of the three opinions, רבא picks the middle one. The buyer gets the field, and the seller keeps only the edge strip on the side he did not list.

keyTerms.meaning: The final law, how we rule

phrases.english: רבא said: the law is:
he acquired everything except the fourth boundary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the three opinions
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In the first version of רבא, the הלכה follows רב: the buyer acquires the whole field except the fourth boundary strip. A second version (Step 11) has רבא ruling like שמואל.

steps.title: Limit: when the fourth boundary is 'swallowed'
steps.stepSummary: רבא's ruling applies only when the fourth boundary sticks out. If it is 'swallowed' inside the space of the other boundaries, the buyer acquires it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: We said this only when it is not swallowed in. But if it is swallowed in, he acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a limit to his own ruling, explaining when the seller does not keep the fourth strip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the fourth side juts out beyond the line formed by the ends of the other boundaries, the seller keeps that strip. If it sits inside that line, it is already covered by the other boundaries, so the buyer gets it.

keyTerms.meaning: We said this only (when...): a phrase that limits a ruling
Swallowed in: included within the other boundaries

steps.whatToRemember: In the first version of רבא: when one boundary is left out, the buyer gets the whole field except that edge strip, and he gets even the strip if it lies inside the other boundaries. Steps 9 to 15 refine this, and Step 11 brings a second version of רבא.

phrases.english: And we said this only where it is not swallowed in,
phrases.notes: Picture the fourth side sticking out past the corners of the neighboring boundaries.

phrases.english: but if it is swallowed in, he acquired it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling given in step 7
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The seller keeps the fourth strip only when it juts out beyond the other boundaries. If it is enclosed within them, the buyer acquires it.

steps.title: Even a strip that sticks out goes to the buyer unless it is important
steps.stepSummary: In the first version, רבא adds a limit: a fourth-boundary strip that sticks out stays with the seller only if it has a row of palm trees or is a nine-קב area. Otherwise the buyer gets it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even when the strip is not swallowed, we only said the buyer does not get it when it has a row of palm trees, or is big enough to sow nine קבין. If it has neither, the buyer acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא narrows his own ruling from Step 8 even further. A strip that sticks out stays with the seller only if it is important.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 8, a strip that sticks out stayed with the seller. Now רבא adds a second condition: the strip must also be worth something, meaning it has a row of palm trees or is a nine-קב area. A small, plain strip goes to the buyer even if it sticks out.

keyTerms.meaning: A row of palm trees growing on the strip
An area big enough to sow nine קבין of seed, so a real, valuable piece of land
'Swallowed', meaning the strip lies inside the line of the other boundaries
'We only said this when…', a phrase that limits a ruling

phrases.english: And even when it is not swallowed
phrases.notes: This continues Step 8. 'Not swallowed' means the fourth-boundary strip sticks out past the other boundaries.

phrases.english: we only said this
where there is a row of palm trees on it,
and it is a nine-kav area;
phrases.notes: Here 'and' works like 'or'. Either one of these makes the strip important.

phrases.english: but if there is no row of palm trees on it,
and it is not a nine-kav area, he acquires it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי לָא מַבְלַע נָמֵי לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limit to רבא's ruling in Step 8
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: First version: a strip that sticks out stays with the seller only if it has a row of palm trees or is a nine-קב area.

steps.title: So a swallowed strip goes to the buyer even if it is important
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws an inference from the first version: if the strip is swallowed, the buyer gets it even with palm trees or a nine-קב area.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can learn from this that when the strip is swallowed, the buyer acquires it even if it has a row of palm trees and is a nine-קב area.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a logical result from what רבא just said about swallowed strips.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's limits only applied to strips that stick out. So in the first version, a swallowed strip always goes to the buyer, no matter how valuable it is.

keyTerms.meaning: 'By implication', meaning we can work out from this that…
Swallowed, lying inside the line of the other boundaries

phrases.english: By implication, when it is swallowed,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיכָּא עֲלֵיהּ רִיכְבָּא דְּדִיקְלָא,
phrases.english: even though there is a row of palm trees on it,
and it is a nine-kav area, he acquires it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the opposite case out of Step 9
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: First version: a swallowed strip always goes to the buyer.

steps.title: Second version: רבא rules like שמואל, but only for a swallowed strip
steps.stepSummary: איכא דאמרי: רבא rules that the buyer gets everything, even the fourth boundary, like שמואל. This applies only when the strip is swallowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רבא said the הלכה is that the buyer acquires everything, even the fourth boundary. But this is only when it is swallowed. If it is not swallowed, he does not acquire it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of רבא's ruling. In this report רבא starts from שמואל's view, not רב's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the strip normally stays with the seller and the buyer gets it only in some cases. In this version it is the other way around: the buyer normally gets it, but not when it sticks out.

keyTerms.meaning: The fourth boundary, the one the seller did not mention

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion. It is a different report of what רבא himself said. The two versions start from opposite sides (רב and שמואל), yet they end up close together.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Rava said: The halakha is:
he acquires everything, even the fourth boundary.
phrases.notes: This is שמואל's view from Step 4.

phrases.english: And we only said this where it is swallowed,
but if it is not swallowed, he does not acquire it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רבא's ruling from Steps 7 to 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Second version: the buyer gets the fourth boundary like שמואל, but only when it is swallowed.

steps.title: Even a swallowed strip stays with the seller if it is important
steps.stepSummary: In the second version, רבא adds that even a swallowed strip goes to the buyer only if it has no row of palm trees and is not a nine-קב area.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even when the strip is swallowed, we only said the buyer gets it when it has no row of palm trees and is not a nine-קב area. If it has palm trees, or is a nine-קב area, he does not acquire it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא narrows the second version: an important strip stays with the seller even when it is swallowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of Step 9. Here the importance test can take a strip away from the buyer even when it is swallowed. In Step 9, the same test worked the other way: a plain, unimportant strip went to the buyer even when it stuck out.

phrases.english: And even when it is swallowed
we only said this
where there is no row of palm trees on it,
and it is not a nine-kav area;
but if there is a row of palm trees on it,
and it is a nine-kav area, he does not acquire it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מַבְלַע נָמֵי לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limit to the second version in Step 11
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Second version: a swallowed strip goes to the buyer only if it is not important.

steps.title: So a strip that sticks out never goes to the buyer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws an inference from the second version: a strip that sticks out stays with the seller even if it is small and plain.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can learn from this that when the strip is not swallowed, the buyer does not acquire it, even if it has no palm trees and is not a nine-קב area.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the logical result of the second version for a strip that sticks out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The importance test in the second version only applied to swallowed strips. So a strip that sticks out always stays with the seller. This is exactly the opposite of the result in Step 10.

phrases.english: By implication, when it is not swallowed,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵיכָּא עֲלֵיהּ רִיכְבָּא דְּדִיקְלָא,
phrases.english: even though there is no row of palm trees on it,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא הָוֵי תִּשְׁעַת קַבִּין – לָא קָנֵי.
phrases.english: and it is not a nine-kav area, he does not acquire it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the opposite case out of Step 12
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Second version: a strip that sticks out always stays with the seller.

steps.title: What both versions of רבא agree on
steps.stepSummary: Both versions agree on three things. The field itself is never held back. A swallowed, unimportant strip goes to the buyer. An important strip that sticks out stays with the seller.
steps.simpleTranslation: From both versions of רבא we learn that the seller held back nothing in the field itself. We also learn that a swallowed strip with no palm trees and no nine-קב area goes to the buyer. A strip that sticks out and has palm trees or a nine-קב area does not go to the buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lines up the two versions and lists the points where they give the same answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions reject רב אסי's idea that the whole field shrinks. They also agree on the two clear-cut cases. They differ only on the mixed cases: a swallowed but important strip, and an unimportant strip that sticks out.

keyTerms.meaning: He held back nothing at all

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree: the field itself always goes to the buyer, a small swallowed strip goes to the buyer, and an important strip that sticks out stays with the seller. The two mixed cases depend on which version you follow.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because the versions agree on these cases, the הלכה is clear in them no matter which version is correct. Only the mixed cases stay in doubt.

phrases.english: We learn from both versions of Rava
that in the field itself he did not hold back anything at all.
And we also learn
that where it is swallowed,
and there is no row of palm trees on it,
and it is not a nine-kav area, he acquires it.
If it is not swallowed,
and there is a row of palm trees on it,
and it is a nine-kav area, he does not acquire it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the two versions of רבא and pulls out the shared rulings
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The field itself is never held back. A swallowed, unimportant strip goes to the buyer. An important strip that sticks out stays with the seller.

steps.title: The two mixed cases are left to the judges
steps.stepSummary: There are two cases where the two versions of רבא disagree: a swallowed strip that is important, and a sticking-out strip that is plain. These are left to the judges' discretion.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the strip is swallowed but has palm trees or a nine-קב area on it, or if it sticks out but has nothing on it, one version rules one way and the other version rules the other way. So it is up to the judges.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the two cases where the two versions of רבא give opposite answers. Since there is no clear ruling, it hands these cases to the judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 listed the cases where both versions agree. These two cases are the leftovers, where the first version gives the strip to the buyer and the second keeps it with the seller. Because we do not know which version is right, the judges decide based on what they think the seller meant.

keyTerms.meaning: swallowed: the strip sits inside the line of the other boundaries
the judges' discretion: the judges decide what fits the case

steps.whatToRemember: Where the two versions of רבא agree, the law is clear. In the two mixed cases (swallowed but important, or sticking out but plain), the judges decide.
steps.confusionAlert: שודא דדייני does not mean the judges may rule however they like. They decide based on what they see as the most likely intention in this case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a standard way the גמרא handles a question it cannot settle: the open cases are handed to the judges.

phrases.english: Swallowed, and there is something on it;
phrases.notes: "Something on it" means a row of palm trees, or an area big enough to plant nine קבין.

phrases.english: not swallowed, and there is nothing on it –
it was stated in this direction,
and it was stated in that direction.
phrases.notes: The two versions of רבא give opposite answers for these two cases.

phrases.english: It is the judges' discretion.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר לַהּ לְהַאי גִּיסָא, וְאִתְּמַר לַהּ לְהַאי גִּיסָא. שׁוּדָא דְּדַיָּינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the comparison begun in Step 14 by dealing with the cases where the versions disagree.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In the disputed mixed cases, the judges decide.

steps.title: Half of my share versus half of the land
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that "the half that I have in the land" sells a full half of the field, but "half of the land that I have" sells only a quarter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: If a man says "the half that I have in the land," he sells half the field. If he says "half of the land that I have," he sells a quarter.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבה rules on two wordings a partner might use when selling, and he says they transfer different amounts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller owns half of a field together with a partner. "The half that I have" points to his whole share, which is half the field. "Half of the land that I have" means half of his share, which is a quarter of the whole field.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
"The half that I have in the land": he sells half.
"Half of the land that I have": he sells a quarter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, still about how the wording of a sale decides what is sold.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "The half that I have" sells a half. "Half of the land that I have" sells a quarter.

steps.title: אביי asks what the difference is, and רבה is silent
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה to explain why the two wordings should be different. רבה does not answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: What is the difference between this wording and that wording? רבה was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבה's ruling, saying the two wordings sound the same. רבה gives no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי feels both sentences just mean "my half," so they should sell the same amount. רבה's silence leaves it unclear whether he gave in or simply chose not to answer. The next step settles this.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא הָכִי וּמַאי שְׁנָא הָכִי?
phrases.english: What is different about this, and what is different about that?
He was silent.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הָכִי וּמַאי שְׁנָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's ruling from Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's distinction between the two wordings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two wordings seem to mean the same thing, so they should sell the same amount.

steps.title: Bills of sale show that רבה kept his ruling
steps.stepSummary: אביי first thought רבה's silence meant he agreed. Later he saw bills of sale from רבה's house written by רבה's rule, which proved he had not changed his mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: I thought that since he was silent, he accepted my view. But that is not so. I saw bills of sale that came out of my master's house, and they were written this way: "the half that I have in the land" means half, and "half of the land that I have" means a quarter.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains what רבה's silence really meant. Bills of sale from רבה's house prove that רבה still held his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Silence could look like agreeing. But real documents written under רבה followed the distinction from Step 16. So רבה's ruling still stands, even though he never answered אביי's question.
steps.confusionAlert: Silence in the גמרא does not always mean someone gave in. Here, what רבה actually did shows he kept his view.

phrases.english: Abaye said: I thought:
since he was silent, he accepted it.
But that is not so;
I saw certain documents
that came out of my master's house,
phrases.notes: "My master" is רבה. The documents were written under his guidance.

phrases.english: and it was written in them like this:
"The half that I have in the land" means half,
"half of the land that I have" means a quarter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אֲנָא סָבְרִי: מִדְּאִישְׁתִּיק – קַבּוֹלֵי קַבְּלַהּ. וְלָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what רבה's silence in Step 17 meant.
steps.raayaObject: That רבה did not take back his ruling from Step 16.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Bills of sale from רבה's house, written by the distinction between the two wordings.

steps.title: A fourth boundary that halves the field, or that sets apart a plot
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that if the fourth boundary is "the land that halves it," the buyer gets half the field. If it is "the land from which a plot is set apart," he gets only a nine-קב area.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה also said: If the fourth boundary is written as "the land through which it is halved," he sells half. If it is written as "the land from which a plot is set apart," he sells nine קבין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives another ruling on wording. This time it is about how the fourth boundary is described in the bill of sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three boundaries are clear, and the fourth is only described in words. "That halves it" sets the line in the middle, so the buyer gets half. "From which a plot is set apart" gives only the smallest piece that counts as a field, which is nine קבין.

keyTerms.meaning: a piece that is cut off or set apart
an area big enough to plant nine קבין of seed

phrases.english: And Rabba said:
"The boundary is the land through which it is halved": he sells half.
phrases.notes: Three sides are marked clearly. This is the wording written for the fourth side.

phrases.english: "The boundary is the land from which a plot is set apart": he sells nine kav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling of רבה on how wording decides the amount sold.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "That halves it" sells half the field. "From which a plot is set apart" sells a nine-קב area.

steps.title: אביי asks why the two boundary wordings should differ
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבה what the real difference is between "the land that halves it" and "the land from which a plot is set apart." רבה does not answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: What is different about this wording, and what is different about that wording? רבה was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבה's boundary ruling from Step 19 by asking why two such similar wordings should lead to such different results. רבה gives no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 19, רבה said one wording gives the buyer half the field, but the other gives him only a nine-קב plot. אביי sees no real difference in meaning between the two phrases, so he asks רבה to justify the split. רבה's silence leaves open whether he is backing down.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? This is a challenge asking for a real difference between two cases.
He was silent and gave no answer.

steps.confusionAlert: This looks just like Steps 17-18, but it is a new challenge. Here אביי is asking about the boundary ruling from Step 19, not the earlier "half that I have" ruling.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
What is different about this wording
and what is different about that wording?
He was silent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: מַאי שְׁנָא הָכִי וּמַאי שְׁנָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's boundary ruling from Step 19, in the same style as אביי's earlier challenge in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that "the land that halves it" gives half the field, but "the land from which a plot is set apart" gives only a nine-קב plot.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two wordings seem to mean the same thing, so they should not lead to such different amounts of land.

steps.title: People conclude from the silence that both wordings give half
steps.stepSummary: From רבה's silence, people conclude that he agreed with אביי, so both wordings would give the buyer half the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: They understood from this that in both this case and that case, the buyer gets half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports what people first concluded from רבה's silence: that he changed his mind. This sets up the next move, where that conclusion will be checked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Silence after a challenge is treated here as a sign that רבה accepted it. If so, the difference from Step 19 is gone, and both wordings give the buyer a full half. This is only a first impression, the same pattern as in Step 18.

keyTerms.meaning: They understood from it. This introduces a conclusion drawn from what just happened.
This one and that one, meaning both cases.

phrases.english: They understood from this,
that both this case and that case get half;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a first conclusion from רבה's silence in Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבה gave up his distinction between the two boundary wordings.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה's silence when אביי challenged him.
